shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving on weathered, granular stone
horizontal bands or registers of repeated motifs
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow, rounded relief with repeated volute-and-disc motifs organised into horizontal bands, and the eroded, granular stone gives a comparable soft, worn quality to the carved lines. The decisive difference is format and composition: A is a tall, freestanding anthropomorphic monument whose ornament is subordinated to a body with head, shoulders and pectoral disc, while B is a low horizontal boulder face bearing a repeating grid-like field of scrolls with no discernible figure.
